statement: NGD equals zero if and only if the probability of local acceptance and global rejection is zero.
domain: Finite probability space with Boolean local and global evaluators
assumptions: The probability of local acceptance is strictly positive.

statement: A constant boundary can have zero NGD on its accepted population while global acceptance does not factor through that boundary.
domain: Two equally probable Boolean trials, constant Unit boundary, fixed continuation
assumptions: Local acceptance and global acceptance both equal the negation of the hidden bit.
